newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan sees first oil swap with Iran in May.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan sees first oil swap with Iran in May.

text.p: A first, landmark oil swap between Kazakhstan and Iran will be completed at the end of May, giving the former Soviet republic much-needed access to oil export markets, the head of state company Kazakh Oil said on Monday.

"On May 29-30, a tanker will anchor at Kharg Island in the Gulf, and Kazakhstan will get its first 70,000 tonnes of oil -- the amount it has already shipped to northern Iran," Nurlan Balgimbayev told a news conference.
Under the deal, resource-rich but landlocked Kazakhstan started shipping its oil across the Caspian Sea to Iran's Caspian coast last December.
In return, Iran must provide the equivalent amount of crude at its Gulf ports -- oil which Kazakhstan then resells on international markets.
"Now we think this project is viable," Balgimbayev said.
The Central Asian country -- five times the size of France and with estimated oil reserves of three billion tonnes -- is anxious to break its reliance on neighbouring Russia for oil exports.
Balgimbayev said that this year Kazakhstan would swap about one million tonnes of crude oil with Iran, adding that volumes would grow to five million tonnes a year in six years.
He said Kazakhstan expected to produce 26.5 million tonnes (530,000 barrels per day) of oil this year, up from 23.5 million (470,000 bpd) last year.
